text:
Lina M: Quick thread — packing pressure shows tiny requests (<=20 tokens) suffer huge p99. Thinking of a cheap fastpath called microgrant: immediate execution slot for tiny reqs with ttl and preempt.

Carlos R: Sounds promising. Two asks: O(1) grant/revoke and token-charge accounting so we don't bleed throughput.

Nora T: Also need hysteresis after preempt to avoid re-grab storms. A small exponential backoff with jitter should work.

Lina M: API sketch: `try_microgrant(max_tokens, ttl_ms)` -> {ok, grant_id}. `revoke(grant_id, mode)` with modes SOFT/FORCE. Record `eviction_reason`.

debug-bot: load-test: microgrant v0 reduced tiny-p99 330ms -> 55ms; throughput -1.6%.

Carlos R: Observability: counters for granted/revoked, hist for backoff_ms, gauge for gpu_delta. Add sampling for high-qps tenants.

Nora T: Impl note: per-worker atomic grant ring + CAS. Signal via eventfd to avoid heavy locks.

Lina M: Risks: large-batch starvation if limits too high; thrash on revoke. Action: RFC + canary config per-route: `microgrant:{enabled, token_limit, max_concurrent, ttl_ms}`.
